unit.title: Reasoning primer: syllogisms and the fallacies that imitate them
unit.question: Which of these arguments actually deduce their conclusions — and which only look like they do?

unit.label: human
unit.definition: A member of the species Homo sapiens.
unit.text: A member of the species Homo sapiens.

unit.label: philosopher
unit.definition: One who pursues wisdom by reasoned inquiry.
unit.text: One who pursues wisdom by reasoned inquiry.

unit.label: wise
unit.definition: Having sound judgement grounded in knowledge.
unit.text: Having sound judgement grounded in knowledge.

unit.label: raining
unit.definition: Water is falling from clouds at the place and time in question.
unit.text: Water is falling from clouds at the place and time in question.

unit.label: fire
unit.definition: Combustion producing flame and heat at the place in question.
unit.text: Combustion producing flame and heat at the place in question.

unit.label: smoke
unit.definition: Visible suspended particles produced by combustion.
unit.text: Visible suspended particles produced by combustion.

unit.label: riverbank
unit.definition: The sloping land alongside a river.
unit.text: The sloping land alongside a river.

unit.label: financial bank
unit.definition: An institution that holds deposits and lends money.
unit.text: An institution that holds deposits and lends money.

unit.label: the ground
unit.definition: The surface of the earth at the place in question.
unit.text: The surface of the earth at the place in question.
If it is raining today, the ground is wet.
If Socrates is a philosopher, then Socrates is wise.
If there is a fire in the kitchen, there is smoke in the kitchen.
There is no fire in the kitchen.
There is no smoke in the kitchen.
Every swan observed in Europe has been white.

unit.title: Barbara: Socrates is mortal
unit.warrant: Universal instantiation of C1 at Socrates, then modus ponens with C2.

unit.title: Modus ponens: the ground is wet
unit.warrant: The conditional R1 and its antecedent R2 yield the consequent.

unit.title: Hypothetical syllogism: every Greek is mortal
unit.warrant: Chaining two universal conditionals through the shared middle term 'human'.

unit.title: Two-step chain: Socrates is mortal via being Greek
unit.warrant: Greek(socrates) gives human(socrates) by C4, which gives mortal(socrates) by C1 — two rule applications, not one.

unit.title: Affirming the consequent
unit.warrant: Runs the conditional backwards: from the consequent to the antecedent.

unit.title: Denying the antecedent
unit.warrant: Infers the negation of the consequent from the negation of the antecedent.

unit.title: Undistributed middle
unit.warrant: Both premises predicate 'human' of their subjects; the middle term is never taken universally, so Greeks and philosophers are never connected.

unit.title: Equivocation on 'bank'
unit.warrant: Looks like Barbara, but 'bank' names a riverbank in E1 and a financial institution in E2.

unit.title: Hasty generalisation: all swans are white
unit.warrant: Every observed swan was white, so all swans are white.

unit.name: affirming_the_consequent
unit.text: S1 licenses wise from philosopher, not philosopher from wise: Socrates could be wise for other reasons.

unit.name: denying_the_antecedent
unit.text: F1 says fire suffices for smoke, not that it is necessary: smoke could come from burnt toast.

unit.name: undistributed_middle
unit.text: 'Human' is the predicate of both premises and distributed in neither, so nothing links Greeks to philosophers.

unit.name: equivocation
unit.text: The word 'bank' shifts sense between the premises; once each sense is written as its own predicate, the conclusion no longer follows.

unit.name: hasty_generalization
unit.text: European observations do not cover the population the conclusion ranges over; black swans live in Australia.
